articleTitle: Integrated Microfluidic Device for Point-of-Care Monitoring of Urinary Cystatin C Levels*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Cystatin C (CysC), an endogenous inhibitor of cysteine proteinases, plays a crucial role as a biomarker in evaluating renal function. Elevated levels of urinary Cystatin C (uCysC) are indicative of tubular dysfunction and injury, potentially signaling the presence of acute kidney injury (AKI). Timely detection of AKI is vital due to its asymptomatic nature and the associated risks. Conventional AKI diagnostic markers like serum creatinine and estimated GFR can be influenced by non-renal factors. In response to the necessity for early AKI detection, a novel microfluidic device designed for rapid and precise uCysC detection is proposed. This microfluidic device presents a simple and user-friendly solution for self-testing and monitoring, adaptable to a variety of environments.

articleTitle: Establishment of a three-dimensional microengineered vascularized endometrium-on-a-chip for the personalized medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Despite of extensive advancements made in research of assisted reproductive technology, many patients still suffer from infertility with unfavorable uterine environment for embryo implantation. The main cause of infertility regarding the endometrium is lack of endometrial receptivity. However, current diagnostics provide insufficient evidence to clinical trials due to the lack of understanding of the molecular features of the receptive endometrium. In this study, we successfully established an endometrium-on-a-chip (EoC), which specializes in mimicking the uterine environment of human and mouse. The reconstructed endometrium in EoCs demonstrated similarity to the in vivo endometrial environment by displaying stage- and diseasespecific cellular and molecular patterns that have been previously reported. Moreover, we developed a novel endometrial receptivity scoring system by quantifying the expression pattern of biochemical markers and vascular development. This scoring system implys the possibility of a refined tool to assess endometrial receptivity in personalized EoCs. In addition, this scoring system showed potential in prediction of IVF-ET success and as a new platform for drug screening. This research represents a significant step towards personalized, evidence-based fertility treatments and the development of advanced diagnostic tools.

articleTitle: Integrated Blood Separation Microfluidic Chip for Prostate-specific Antigen (PSA) Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Prostate-specific antigen (PSA) is one of the most important biomarkers for the diagnosis and prognosis of prostate cancer. This paper reports an integrated self-driven microfluidic diagnostic chip for PSA detection, which is designed to simplify the entire procedure from whole blood sample input to quantitative PSA concentration output. We integrated three technologies into one single device: automatic blood plasma separation by the membrane, on-chip microparticle reaction, and microparticle accumulation for result visualization. Sequential capillary draining is utilized to extract blood plasma separated by the membrane and also to control the flow sequence and velocity of different solutions to achieve a highly efficient reaction [1, 2].

articleTitle: Herceptin-Positive Breast Cancer Treatment via Immunoliposomes Triggered by High-Frequency Ultrasound and Microbubbles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: abstract-Functionalizing chemotherapeutics-loaded liposomes with monoclonal antibodies can enhance their specificity and minimize side effects. Targeting the human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), overexpressed in HER2-positive breast cancer, is achievable by coating liposomes with an anti-HER2 monoclonal antibody. This study focused on synthesizing doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded immunoliposomes functionalized with anti-HER2 (HER-lip). The release of the drug from these immunoliposomes was triggered by high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) and microbubbles, which acted as exogenous cavitation-enhancing agents. The platform was evaluated for size, lipid content, protein concentration, stability, and controlled release profiles. In vitro assessments were also performed, including the MTT assay for cell viability and flow cytometry to evaluate drug uptake. This innovative drug delivery system shows potential for combined therapeutic and diagnostic applications, improving personalized cancer care and treatment

articleTitle: Effect of Ultrasound and Mixing of Folate and Trastuzumab Liposomes on DOX Release and Cellular Uptake
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: This study explores the potential of physically mixing individually targeted Doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded liposomes functionalized with folic acid (FA) and trastuzumab (TRA), combined with ultrasound (US) triggering, to enhance targeted breast cancer therapy. This research focused on synthesizing, characterizing, and evaluating DOX release, cellular uptake, and cytotoxicity of FA-PEG and TRA-PEG-modified liposomes mixed at different volume fractions. Low-frequency ultrasound (LFUS) and high-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) were employed to trigger DOX release. The study demonstrated that the sonicated-physically-mixed liposomes showed superior release performance (specifically the M75 group) and increased cellular uptake (specifically the M25 group) compared to individually targeted liposomes, highlighting their combined potential in breast cancer treatment.

articleTitle: Image Processing Algorithm for Porphyromonas gingivalis Outer Membrane Vesicle Transport in Periodontal Pathogenesis*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Porphyromonas gingivalis (Pg) is a key pathogen in periodontal disease, releasing outer membrane vesicles (OMV) enriched with small RNAs (sRNA). This study presents an image processing algorithm that combines density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise (DBSCAN) and polar coordinate conversion to identify and track the OMV movement within host cells, which is crucial for understanding their role in disease pathogenesis. Preliminary results indicate effective tracking and visualizing of OMV trajectories during endocytosis, providing insights into OMV-sRNA delivery mechanisms and their impact on host cell function.

Index Terms: Role In The Pathogenesis Of Diseases

articleTitle: Determining Low Concentrations of Silver Ions from measurements of DC Conductivity of Highly Insulating Liquid Media by the Alternate Polarization Current Method*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Driven by many applications, the development of new biomaterials has considerably increased in the last decade. Silver, and particularly silver nanoparticles (AgNPs) have gained popularity in the biomedical domain due to their inherent antimicrobial properties. Beyond the validation of their efficiency, achievement of sustainable applications of AgNPs-tailored antimicrobial surfaces implies knowledge on the released amount of ionic silver $\left(\mathrm{Ag}^{+}\right) / \mathbf{A g N P s}$ in order to control their biocidal/toxicity level and prevent from users and environmental risks. To that end, we propose here a reliable approach for measuring DC conductivity of highly insulating liquid media (water solutions containing low concentrations of silver ions) by using the alternate polarization current method. The current, which is related to the conductivity of the media, is measured in the $10^{-14}$ to $10^{-5} \mathrm{~A}$ range with high accuracy (dispersion less than 2%). The amount of silver ions $\left(\mathbf{A g}^{+}\right)$ is then determined.

articleTitle: Surface Modification of 3D Printed Biomedical Scaffolds Through an Electron Beam Processe
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: This study introduces a method for employing electron beam processing to effectuate both physical and chemical modifications to the surface of 3D printed biomedical scaffolds. Generally, 3D printed scaffolds exhibit certain limitations, including rough surface textures and dimensional inaccuracies, which hinder their applicability in medical contexts. To mitigate these issues, we implemented the electron beam technique to enhance surface smoothness and facilitate chemical alterations. The proposed method is not only efficient in polishing the surfaces of the printed scaffolds but also capable of processing a substantial number of samples within a brief timeframe. This technique holds potential for various biomedical implant devices and can be adapted for use with a range of metallic materials and polymer printing. Notably, the electron beam process described herein relies solely on heat treatment via electron application, thereby ensuring the complete elimination of any potential adverse effects that may arise during clinical trials related to the materials used.

articleTitle: A Neurostimulator with Wireless Bidirectional Communication for Controlling Muscle Contraction Force using Electromyography
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: This paper presents a wirelessly powered neurostimulator with wireless bidirectional communication to control muscle contraction. The transmitter device sends the information about neural stimulation to the receiver device, while the receiver device sends the measured electromyography (EMG) inside a body to the transmitter device. Based on the measured EMG, the neural stimulation was adjusted to achieve the target EMG. The muscle contraction force can be controlled by EMG control. The EMG estimation error by the developed device was less than 2% when the muscle activity was active. This study can contribute to force control of paralyzed patients’ bodies.

articleTitle: Enhancing Cardiomyocyte Maturation via Mechanical Stimulation of 3D Printed Cardiac Tissue Using a Origami-based 3D Sensor and Magnetic Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Drug-induced cardiotoxicity remains a major obstacle in early drug development, underscoring the need for more advanced preclinical methods to identify cardiotoxic risks. Traditional in vitro cardiac models often fail to replicate the complex physiological characteristics of adult cardiomyocytes and rely heavily on image-based methods for contractility assessments, which can lack precision. In this study, we introduce a novel 3D sensor platform that integrates magnetic micro-rods and gold strain sensors on a polyimide substrate, forming a 3D structure through buckling assembly. This innovative system not only provides precise mechanical stimulation but also enables real-time monitoring of contractile forces in 3D cardiac tissues, significantly improving the fidelity and accuracy of cardiotoxicity screening. Evaluations of the system demonstrated its robustness and stability, while the incorporation of 3D bioprinting technology allowed for the direct cultivation of engineered cardiac tissues on the sensor, enhancing its applicability for preclinical testing and drug development.

articleTitle: Feasibility of using ultrasound for drug delivery through micellar systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: A study of micellar structures subjected to continuous high-intensity ultrasonic perturbation was carried out. The micelles were characterized by high-speed absorption spectrophotometry and the use of fluorophores, such as Rhodamine 123, as a spectroscopic indicator of the micellar kinetic process. It was found that above the critical micellar concentration, the absorbance peak of the fluorophore experiences a 14 nm red shift. Preliminary experiments indicate a reversal of this shift under certain ultrasonic conditions. In subsequent experiments, no effect of high intensity ultrasonic radiation on the micellar systems studied was observed. A dependence of the spectroscopic response of Rh123 on temperature is found, which can be confused with the effect of micelle breaking in solutions. The study presented considers the use of Quillaja Saponaria Molina and Triton X-100 as a surfactant, but it is extensible to other micellar systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Effects of Cyclic Hypoxia on Vascular Permeability Using Microfluidic Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Ischemic conditioning reportedly improves tissue tolerance to ischemic injury by affecting vascular function through changes in oxygen concentration. However, the detailed mechanisms and effective procedures have not yet been clarified. In this study, we investigated functional changes in the microvascular network and underlying mechanisms, focusing on the generation of reactive oxygen species (ROS). A microvascular network formed in a microfluidic device was exposed to oxygen concentrations of either 21% or $0.3 \% \mathrm{O}_{2}$, as well as cyclic hypoxic condition ranging between 0.3% and $21 \% \mathrm{O}_{2}$ at $30-\mathrm{min}$ intervals for 3 h. Vascular permeability after cyclic hypoxic condition decreased significantly compared to those under the two constant oxygen conditions. Moreover, ROS generation fluctuated in response to the variation in the oxygen concentration under cyclic hypoxic condition, and remained relatively high. Thus, cyclic hypoxia alters microvascular network function in a manner similar to ischemic conditioning and is associated with sustained ROS generation.

articleTitle: Lipid Imaging Inside Infrared-Transparent Microfluidic Channel Using Fourier Transform Infrared (μFTIR) Microspectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Several pathologies ranging from cardiovascular diseases to metabolic syndromes can be characterized by a high saturated lipids to unsaturated lipids ratio. In this study, we demonstrate the feasibility of Infrared (IR) micro-spectroscopy based chemical imaging to perform both imaging and saturated/unsaturated discrimination of lipids inside microfluidic devices. We present data collected for imaging lipids flown inside 9-micron thick IR transparent microfluidic channels in the form of whole liquid columns and lipid microdroplets using Fourier Transform Infrared (μFITR) Micro-spectroscopy imaging.

articleTitle: A Molecular Self-Assembly AFM Nanoprinting System Towards the Fabrication of Functional Technorganic Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Here, we demonstrate liquid-liquid interface molecular self-assembly (MSA) protocols to fabricate functional technorganic machines. Utilizing a custom-built 3D nanoprinting system that integrates scanning probe microscopy, microfluidics, mechatronics, and specialized surface chemistry, we achieved the spontaneous deposition of hierarchical molecular carbon nanosheets-the first of its kind for liquid-liquid MSA. A successfully fabricated mesoscale structure was verified through optical microscopy, SEM, and microCT imaging, confirming the system’s feasibility. Towards addressing the challenge of achieving in-situ nanoprinting feedback and control while using opaque substrates necessitated by MSA, we conceptualized an Electro-Femtofluidic Flow Sensor which we demonstrated is theoretically capable of femtoliter-per-second flow rate measurements, a capability which has not yet been demonstrated in the field. These advancements establish new nanofabrication methods, enabling the creation of molecular-level machines with diverse functionalities for applications in medicine and beyond.

articleTitle: Assessing the Effects of Gas Insufflation on Compromised Blood Vessels Using Vascular Systems-on-Chip
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: Gas insufflation is a procedure used in many medical interventions, such as laparoscopy. This study investigates the uptake of gas as a result of gas insufflation in the near vicinity of small blood vessels presenting submillimeter, often-invisible fissures. Because gas uptake is entirely a physical process, the microvasculature could be mimicked by an abiotic, polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) made microfluidics system, comprising microchannels simulating small blood vessels, with widths of $30 \mu \mathrm{~m}, 50 \mu \mathrm{~m}, \mathbf{8 0} \mu \mathrm{~m}$, or $250 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, hosting the flow of synthetic blood at rates similar to those experienced in human body. The artificial blood vessels presented perforations with either $16 \mu \mathrm{~m}, 32 \mu \mathrm{~m}$, or $100 \mu \mathrm{~m}$ widths, positioned between the pressure chamber, where gas insufflation occurs, and the artificial blood vessels. Air was injected into the pressure chamber at rates similar to those used in laparoscopy, i.e., ranging from $10 \mathrm{~mL} / \mathrm{h}$ to $100 \mathrm{~mL} / \mathrm{h}$. The characteristics of bubbles due to gas uptake in the blood stream were correlated with perforation sizes, artificial blood vessel widths, and insufflation rates. Bubble volumes, particularly the maximum bubble volumes, increased proportionally with the width of the artificial blood vessel and the flow rate of the blood. As the artificial blood vessel width increased, the bubbles exhibited increasingly chaotic behavior, indicated by greater variability in bubble volumes. Larger perforations translated in an increased risk of gas embolism phenomena. Finally, higher injection rates intensified the chaotic character and simultaneously increased the total bubble volumes. These findings underscore possible significant risks associated with gas insufflation and similar procedures involving gas introduction, particularly for patients with damaged or compromised vascular systems.

articleTitle: Microbial Classification by Multimodal Atomic Force Microscopy with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 17th International Conference on Nano/Molecular Medicine & Engineering (NANOMED)
abstract: The development of high-purity sterile environments is essential in healthcare, and the maintenance of environments. Monitoring microbial conditions is a critical process during disinfection, especially for highly resistant endospores, which can induce re-contamination under suitable triggers. Traditional optical-based microbial detection techniques struggle with resolution and effectiveness and lack the multi-parametric information. We introduce automated AFM with multimodal ML integration to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of microbial detection. This approach leverages detailed mechanical data from AFM, coupled with the analytical capabilities of ML, to provide a more robust method for identifying microorganisms in complex environments. Overall, the work aims to improve the efficiency and accuracy of AFM through robotic technology and artificial intelligence, and freeing researchers from the labor of time-consuming measurements and data analysis.
